item.title: Contracts and legal language
item.description: Formal language for agreements, terms and obligations.

children.definition: to state clearly that something must be done, as part of an agreement or rule
children.example: The contract stipulates that payment must be made within 30 days.

children.definition: that must be obeyed because of a law or agreement
children.example: Once signed, the agreement is legally binding.

children.definition: legal responsibility for something, especially costs or damage
children.example: The airline accepts no liability for valuables left in checked luggage.

children.definition: an act of breaking a law, rule or agreement
children.example: Sharing client data would be a breach of contract.

children.definition: a separate section of a legal document
children.example: A confidentiality clause prevents staff from discussing the deal.

children.definition: to choose not to demand something you have a right to
children.example: The bank agreed to waive the late payment fee.

children.definition: to end something formally, such as a contract
children.example: Either side may terminate the agreement with 60 days' notice.
The court declared the contract null and void.

children.definition: following a rule, law or someone's wishes
children.example: Your data will be deleted in accordance with company policy.

children.definition: the official power to make legal decisions, or the area where this power applies
children.example: The case falls outside the court's jurisdiction.

children.definition: one of the people or organisations involved in a legal agreement
children.example: Both parties signed the agreement on Monday.

children.definition: to promise to pay for any loss or damage that someone may suffer
children.example: The client agrees to indemnify the agency against any claims.
